entries.title: The match day, tightened up
bullets: The score and the match stay at the top of the screen while you scroll, with the latest moment underneath and a thin bar showing how far through the match it is.
Everything else sits below: the controls (now in two tidy rows), kick-off and the half-time call, the paper and the report, the other scores and the commentary. The stats are at the very bottom.
A smaller scoreboard and tighter controls mean the whole first half fits on one phone screen. The match itself is the same size as before.
Fixed: the half-time and full-time stats table showed the team names in a column away from their numbers.

entries.title: A nudge to the home screen
bullets: On a phone, once you’ve played your first match, the game offers to go on your home screen, with the steps for your phone and the icon to look for at each one. Not now, and it asks again in a few days, three times at most; or tap Don’t ask again.
On an iPhone or iPad it reminds you first to save your career to the cloud, because the home-screen game keeps its own saves.

entries.title: Play from your home screen
bullets: Put Title Push on your home screen and it opens like an app, full screen. On Android, tap Install on the title screen (or in Club → Save); on an iPhone or iPad, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
The home-screen game always opens the newest playtest, and once you’ve played it, it opens without a signal too.
Left open while a new playtest goes up, the game tells you, and Reload brings it in. It never reloads by itself in the middle of a match.
On an iPhone or iPad, the home-screen game keeps its own saves, apart from the browser’s. Use cloud saves to take a career across.
The game has an icon now, in the browser tab too.

entries.title: What’s in the game, brought up to date
bullets: The title screen’s list of what’s in the game now includes cloud saves and matchday sound, and no longer says your game saves in this browser only. Online leagues, cloud saves and the crowd’s sound are off the Coming Soon list; music is still to come.

entries.title: The end of a match
bullets: The players no longer freeze at the final whistle. A narrow win ends with the winners running together to celebrate while the beaten side trudge off; a draw ends in handshakes. At half time everyone walks off, and the referee takes the ball.
When your side scores, the fans in the stands throw their arms in the air.
Arms raised look right now: the keeper’s dive reaches past his head, and the referee holds a card up high.

entries.title: Open leagues and friends
bullets: Open leagues: a league can be open to anyone. It’s listed under Open leagues, where any manager can find it and join, no link needed. Or keep it to people with the link.
Friends: everyone has a friend code. Add a friend by their code or link, and once they accept you can invite each other to leagues. Invites wait for them under Leagues with friends.

entries.title: Leagues with friends
bullets: Leagues with friends: make a competition, send your friends the link, and each of you runs a club in one shared world. Sign in with the same account as cloud saves.

The matches play at a deadline, once or twice a day, one to five matches at a time. Before it, use the screens you know (your team, plan book, training, ground, transfers and money) and it all goes in as your orders.
After the deadline everyone sees the same results, and you can watch the highlights of your matches. Miss three deadlines in a row and your club runs itself until you’re back.

entries.title: What the coach thinks would have happened
bullets: After a match, your assistant may tell you what would have happened with one thing different: the style or formation that beats theirs, the half-time call you didn’t make, or (in a match you watch) the shout. It’s worked out by playing the same match again that way.
He’s honest about it: “we’d have won that” only when the replay was clearly better, “might have, could be luck” when it wasn’t, and when nothing would have saved it, he says so.
For a match you skip, the line appears with the last result on the main menu.

entries.title: Counting visits to the website
bullets: The website now counts visits, anonymously: no cookies, nothing about you, and nothing at all if your browser asks not to be tracked. The game opened from your own computer never counts.

entries.title: Let the club build the ground
bullets: Let the club build your ground. On the Ground page, or when you start a career, choose who builds it: you, or the club. The club builds what the next grade needs first, then what the fans are short of, sets fair prices and never spends you into the red. It pays a contractor 15% on top and won’t squeeze the most out of a sell-out, so a ground you design yourself can earn more.

entries.title: Shouts without stopping the match
bullets: Touchline shouts no longer stop the match. At 60′ and 75′ the shout pops up over the pitch while play goes on, and the clock slows down while it’s open so you have time to choose.
A shout takes effect from the end of the five minutes being played. Press nothing and the team carries on as it is.
Fixed: the match showed “Full time” at 60′ and 75′.

entries.title: Matchday sound and cloud saves
bullets: Matchday sound. The crowd murmurs, rises as the ball nears the box, roars at a goal and groans at a miss; you hear the ball, the net, the post and the referee’s whistle, and the rain when it’s raining. It’s all made by the game itself. Turn it off with the Sound switch by the match controls.
The training on the title screen and the hub joins the session part-way through, at a different drill each time, so it isn’t always the warm-up laps.
Cloud saves. Sign in with an email and password, or with Google, under Club → Save, and your career goes online: an autosave at the end of each week, and three slots of your own.
Carry on in another browser. Sign in on the title screen and load your career from the cloud.
The cloud never overwrites something you haven’t seen. If your cloud autosave came from another device, or is a different career, the game asks before replacing it.
The game still saves on your device, signed in or not, and plays offline.

entries.title: Expected points, graded grounds and What’s New
bullets: Expected points in the season review. Every match now keeps its expected goals, and the review says how many points your chances were worth against the points you got.
Other clubs’ grounds are graded by the same rules as yours. A club that hasn’t built what the tier above needs can’t go up, and the League table says what its ground is missing.
What’s New. This panel opens once after each new playtest, with the version history underneath. Open it again from the title screen or the footer.
The title screen and the footer show which playtest version you’re playing, and when it was built.

entries.title: League trends
bullets: League trends on the Tactics screen. A new card shows which styles and formations the league is playing this season, with the top three of each and how often each one is used.
A headline when one style dominates. When one style is in at least 30% of game plans, you’ll see something like “High Press is everywhere this season”. Otherwise it says “No style dominates”.
How to beat the trend. The card names what counters the most common style and formation, for example “Counter or Long Ball beat High Press”.
No trend early in the season. It waits until about two rounds have been played before calling one.
Results are unchanged. The card only shows information, so no results or match numbers changed.

entries.title: The formation cycle
bullets: Formation rock-paper-scissors cycle: wide forwards beat midfield 4/5, midfield 4/5 beats back 3/5, and back 3/5 beats wide forwards.
The Tactics screen, opponent habits, the match report’s “Next time” tip, and half-time notes explain the cycle.

entries.title: The first public playtest
bullets: The game is called Title Push.
A match report at full time: what went right, what went wrong, how lucky the finishing was, and a “Next time” tip.
Opponent habits on the Tactics screen: what this week’s opponent usually plays, how to counter it, and how your shape lines up against theirs.
Half-time choices: take the coach’s advice, stick with your own plan, or set orders for each kind of score and let the coach call it.
Touchline shouts at 60 and 75 minutes, to push for a goal or shut the game down.
A plan-book editor, and a line saying which plan this week’s match will use.
Away grounds drawn to the size of the home club’s ground.
Club → Save → “Export playtest timings” records how long you spent on each screen, to send with your feedback.

entries.title: Matchday crowds and the season wrap
bullets: Fans walk to their place on matchday: queue, mood, crowding and sales overlays on the ground, and a replay of the day.
Catering prices and staffing, and matchday programmes.
Split a stand into sections, or join two stands into one.
Tips for your first season.
A season review, with your best signing, and the story of twenty seasons with an all-time XI.
Weather and floodlights in the match, corner stands, and the same colours for stands in the builder and the match.
Easier to use on a phone and with a keyboard or screen reader.

entries.title: Your ground in the match
bullets: Top-down match highlights with smoother action, a goal replay, and a button to skip to the next highlight.
The stands you built appear around the pitch in your home matches.
A test bed to watch any level of football, from the top flight to the Sunday league.

entries.title: The career and the first look
bullets: A playable career: league, cup, tactics, squad and saves, in a portrait pixel-art look with styles to switch between.
Backroom staff whose advice is only as good as they are.
Money and a starting ground, built tile by tile, with ticket prices and season tickets.
Transfers and contracts, and club facilities.
Decisions in your inbox.
A single-file build to play from disk, and a Coming Soon list of what isn’t in yet.
